headline: Powerful earthquake leaves villages cut off

sources.title: Rescuers struggle to reach Colombia earthquake epicenter (CNN)
Colombia earthquake 2026: What you need to know (CARE)
Colombia rescue efforts press on after deadly earthquake (video, France 24 English)

chunks.text: Just after [[dawn]] on August 10, the ground in western Colombia began to shake. The earthquake, with a [[magnitude]] of 7.4, was one of the strongest in the country's modern history. People {{rushed out}} of their homes in cities as far away as Bogota and Medellin, and the [[shaking]] was felt in Ecuador and Panama. In several cities, buildings {{came down}}, and more than 290 people [[lost their lives]].

verbs.correct: To leave a place very fast
verbs.wrong: To lock the doors and hide
verbs.why: Students rush out when a fire alarm rings, and shoppers rush out of a store during a sale. People in Bogota and Medellin rushed out of their homes the moment the ground began to shake.

verbs.wrong: To shake from side to side
verbs.why: A tree branch can come down in a strong wind, and an old chimney might come down during a storm. Several buildings in western Colombia came down when the magnitude 7.4 earthquake struck.

chunks.text: The worst problems are in Choco, a [[region]] of mountains and deep forest near the [[epicenter]]. The quake {{set off}} [[landslides]] that [[buried]] the roads, and some villages were completely {{cut off}}: no cars, no trucks, no help. [[Rescue teams]] are trying to {{get through}} to them, but with the roads gone, even reaching the smallest towns can take days. Helicopters may be the only [[way in]].

verbs.why: A dropped match can set off a grass fire, and heavy rain can set off a flood warning downtown. The earthquake set off landslides that buried the mountain roads leading into Choco.

Deep snow can cut off a mountain town for days, and a flood can cut off the only bridge to a farm. Several villages near the epicenter were completely cut off, with no cars, no trucks, and no way to reach them.

Snowplows work all night so trucks can get through after a blizzard, and climbers sometimes cannot get through in a storm. Rescue teams are trying to get through to villages the landslides left blocked.

chunks.text: Closer to the cities, the rescue work never stops. Neighbors and [[firefighters]] {{dug out}} [[survivors]] from under fallen walls with [[bare hands]] and [[shovels]]. Rescuers work [[day and night]] and refuse to {{give up}} while people are still missing. Every person pulled from the [[rubble]] brings new energy to the teams.

verbs.correct: To free someone from under things
verbs.wrong: To carry someone to a doctor
verbs.why: Rescuers dig out a climber trapped in deep snow, and villagers can dig out a car buried by a storm. Neighbors and firefighters dug out survivors from under fallen walls using only bare hands and shovels.
A tired runner might give up before the finish line, and a team can give up after falling far behind. Rescuers in Colombia refuse to give up while anyone is still missing under the rubble.

chunks.text: The government {{stepped in}} within hours and declared a [[state of emergency]]. [[Aid workers]] {{hand out}} clean water, food, and [[blankets]], and neighbors share what little they have. More than 140 people are still [[missing]], so [[officials]] fear the number of dead may {{go up}}. Many families lost everything and must now {{start over}} and slowly [[rebuild]] their lives. For them, the rescue workers who keep arriving are a reason to hope.

verbs.correct: To act to help in a problem
verbs.why: A referee steps in to stop a fight, and a manager can step in when a project is late. Colombia's government stepped in within hours and declared a state of emergency for the affected region.

verbs.correct: To give things to many people
verbs.wrong: To sell things at low prices
verbs.why: Volunteers hand out soup at a shelter, and an airline hands out water during a long delay. Aid workers in Colombia hand out clean water, food, and blankets to families who lost everything.
Bread prices go up every month at the market, and a fever can go up quickly overnight. Colombian officials fear the number of dead may go up as more people are found in the rubble.
A bakery starts over after a fire destroys the kitchen, and a family can start over after losing a home. Many families in Choco lost everything and must now start over, slowly rebuilding their lives.

mainIdea.s: A powerful earthquake hit western Colombia, and landslides left mountain villages cut off. Rescuers are working day and night to reach and free survivors.
mainIdea.why: The magnitude 7.4 quake killed more than 290 people, buried roads in Choco, and rescue teams are still trying to get through.

mainIdea.s: A powerful earthquake shook Colombia, but the rescue work is already finished. Roads reopened within a day, and every missing person has now been found safe.
mainIdea.why: Close, but the rescue is far from finished. Villages are still cut off, and more than 140 people are missing.

mainIdea.s: Colombia has opened a national center that teaches families how to prepare for earthquakes. Visitors practice safety drills inside a special shaking room.
mainIdea.why: The article is about a real earthquake and the rescue effort, not about a safety training center.

lines.text: Colombia was hit by one of the strongest earthquakes in its modern history. Magnitude 7.4, just after dawn.
More than 290 people have died. People {{rushed out}} of their homes as far away as Bogota, and in several cities buildings {{came down}}.
Choco, a region of mountains and deep forest near the epicenter. The quake {{set off}} landslides that buried the roads, and some villages are completely {{cut off}}. No cars, no trucks, no help.
How do rescuers even reach them?
They're trying to {{get through}}, but with the roads gone it can take days. Helicopters may be the only way in.
The rescue work never stops. Neighbors and firefighters {{dug out}} survivors with bare hands and shovels, and the teams refuse to {{give up}} while people are still missing.
More than 140, so officials fear the number of dead may {{go up}}.
It {{stepped in}} within hours and declared a state of emergency. Aid workers {{hand out}} water, food, and blankets, and neighbors share [[what little they have]].
[[That last part gets me]]. People with almost nothing, still sharing.
